extracted.intended_audience: public relations / communications professionals and organizational PR staff writing award announcement press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting an award-announcement press release: required elements, recommended structure (headline, lead, body, quotes, boilerplate, contact), length, timing, and quality checks to make the release newsworthy and journalist-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action-oriented headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline that conveys significance immediately and prompts interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys significance immediately; includes specific award name; includes organization name; 10-15 words maximum; action-oriented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary line that provides details that didn't fit in the headline and gives journalists a reason to keep reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to add details such as consecutive streak, competitive pool size, rank, category count. Example: "Recognition marks fifth consecutive year on the program's annual list."

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Ws first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead paragraph (two to three sentences) that answers Who, Which award, When, Where, and Why the subject was selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer: who won; which award; when; where; why selected (criteria). Write in third person throughout. Keep it concise and newsy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award credibility paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph establishing the credibility of the awarding organization and legitimacy of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background on the awarding organization and selection criteria details so readers understand award authority and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievement details
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific description of what the recipient did to earn the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what specifically earned the recognition and include the recipient's relevant background and accomplishments; make clear why the achievement is notable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two meaningful quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include two substantive, non-braggy quotes offering distinct perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One quote from the recipient and one from a senior executive at your organization (or alternatively one from the awarding organization's leader). Quotes should be insightful, not mere praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard organizational boilerplate that describes the issuing association or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the short, consistent paragraph about the organization (what it is, mission, brief background) that journalists can reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear press contact details so journalists can follow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, title, phone number, email and any relevant social handles or PR contact pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body / Background and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle section of the release providing supporting context beyond the lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include background on the awarding organization, selection criteria details, what specifically earned the recognition, recipient's relevant background, and industry context to explain significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall length and document scope for the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep between 300-500 words and fit on one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words to drop / avoid self-aggrandizement
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid canned self-promotional phrases and inflated adjectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use phrases like "Proud to announce" or adjectives like "prestigious" — let the award name speak for itself. Avoid overt self-aggrandizement and fluff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When to distribute the release for maximum relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute immediately after award announced (24-48 hours). If attending a ceremony, distribute day of or after. Aim for the award's peak relevance window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award name and source clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the award name and the awarding organization unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the full award name and awarding body early (headline/lead) so readers instantly understand what was won and by whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific selection criteria mentioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state the criteria used to select the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the evaluation or selection criteria so journalists and readers understand the basis for the recognition (e.g., innovation, impact, growth metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Why the winner deserved it
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain convincingly the reasons the recipient was selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete evidence or examples of accomplishments, outcomes, or impact that justify the selection rather than vague praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry context (significance of award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the award and recipient within broader industry or market context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the award's relevance to the industry, why it matters, and how it reflects on trends or standards in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two perspectives (recipient + awarding body)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include at least two viewpoints to add depth and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quotes or statements representing both the recipient and the awarding organization (or your org) to show both accomplishment and external validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fluff or self-praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep tone factual and journalistic rather than promotional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hyperbole, unsupported superlatives, and marketing copy; focus on newsworthy facts and verifiable achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: News value beyond 'we won'
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the release communicates newsworthy elements that matter to external audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show broader impact, novelty, competitive context, milestones (e.g., first, largest, consecutive years) or other elements that make the story relevant beyond internal stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Include images or media that support coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality awards photos, recipient headshots, or other visual assets to increase pickup by media.
